DAY 109-111 — MAJOR CORRECTION: THE MOU WAS SIGNED 2 DAYS EARLY, AT VERSAILLES, NOT BURGENSTOCK. Wednesday June 17 evening: President Trump PERSONALLY SIGNED the US-Iran memorandum of understanding during a state dinner at the Palace of Versailles, France (G7 sidelines), with French President Macron standing beside him. IRAN'S PRESIDENT MASOUD PEZESHKIAN also signed in person — distinct from the earlier digital signing Sunday Jun 15 by VP Vance and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf. PAKISTAN PM SHEHBAZ SHARIF confirmed: 'Islamabad MoU shall enter into force with immediate effect and, as a first step, the Islamic Republic of Iran will instantly reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the United States of America will immediately lift the naval blockade.' Sharif praised both Khamenei and Pezeshkian for 'wisdom, foresight and statesmanship.' THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION REVEALED THE 14-POINT MOU IN FULL Wednesday: (1) Immediate/permanent end to war on all fronts including Lebanon. (2) Mutual sovereignty respect, non-interference. (3) Hormuz: Iran's lead negotiator Ghalibaf said the strait 'will NOT return to pre-war conditions' — Iran will 'receive a fee for services' to shipping, meaning the PGSA toll framework persists in modified form. (4) Nuclear: Iran 'reaffirms it shall not procure or develop nuclear weapons'; enriched uranium to be 'down-blended on site under the supervision of the IAEA' via a mechanism still to be 'mutually agreed.' (5) $300 BILLION FUND DENIED: Trump — 'not investing 10 cents' — the deal instead permits THIRD-PARTY investment into Iran contingent on compliance, not a direct US fund (refuting earlier FT/Iranian-media reports). KHAMENEI AUTHORISED THE DEAL THURSDAY despite holding 'a different view,' after assurances from Pezeshkian that Iran's rights and 'Resistance Front' interests would be protected; Pezeshkian/SNSC pledged not to yield to 'excessive' future US demands. US LAWMAKERS (both parties) flagged concerns: nuclear verification mechanism undefined, Iran's missile programme not addressed. Trump will send the deal to Congress. IAEA DIRECTOR GROSSI: 'It is good that the memorandum is there. Now the technical work starts.' BURGENSTOCK TODAY (FRIDAY JUN 19): NOT a signing ceremony — Al Jazeera confirms documents 'already signed,' today is 'the official kickoff of the 59 days remaining for these sides to come to a conclusion.' Venue: Burgenstock Resort, Stansstad, near Lucerne, owned by Qatar's Katara Hospitality (same 2024 Ukraine peace summit venue). Vance + Ghalibaf attending. BRENT FRIDAY: $78.31 (-1.6%). WTI: $74.75 (-1.7%) — still above pre-war ~$70 given residual uncertainty on Hormuz administration mechanism and verification details. US stock futures surged Wed evening on the surprise signing. West Asia War Day 111: THE WAR IS FORMALLY OVER; A 60-DAY FINAL-SETTLEMENT NEGOTIATION BEGINS TODAY.

assessment.body:
Thursday 7:45 AM IST. Day 138. Blockade day 2.

THE 48-HOUR PICTURE
• Jul 14 (Tue): Trump dropped the 20% Hormuz toll after Gulf objections — replaced with trade-and-investment pledges. Blockade resumed 4 PM ET (Wed 1:30 AM IST). A fourth consecutive night wave — 7 hours, dozens of targets. Iran struck a US air base in Jordan; Qeshm Island hit; Kuwait intercepted incoming twice in 30 minutes.
• Jul 15 (Wed): Blockade day 1 — 2 vessels redirected, 1 non-compliant tanker disabled off Kharg Island. Strikes moved to daylight: Greater Tunb Island (90 minutes), then Bandar Abbas command centres and coastal defences. Iranian figures: 7+ troops killed in a barracks strike, 30+ civilians dead, 260+ wounded — unverified. The IRGC threatened all regional energy exports; a Houthi official threatened a coordinated Bab el-Mandeb closure.
• Off-ramps stayed open: Iran released a detained American; Vance ruled out ground troops and regime change; Ghalibaf kept diplomacy alive even as the foreign ministry said no talks are planned.

INDIA IMPACT
• The transmission channel has shifted from equities to the currency and prices: rupee past 96 for the first time since May (96.16 Tue, 96.32 Wed; options pricing a test of 96.50), and June WPI at 9.87% — the war is now in wholesale inflation.
• Equities are absorbing it: Wednesday closed green (+130 pts) despite $85 Brent and daytime strikes; VIX eased to ~13.1. FII sold Rs 739.69 Cr Tuesday, returned to financials Wednesday. Thursday: cautious open signalled.
• Brent ~$85.9 — OMC under-recovery re-opening; a sustained $85+ plus a 96-handle rupee makes an August fuel revision increasingly likely.
• The Bab el-Mandeb threat matters uniquely for India: it would hit Red Sea-Suez trade on top of Hormuz energy exposure — a two-chokepoint squeeze.

ASSESSMENT
• The contest is now formalised: a US port blockade plus 'guardian angel' control claim versus Iran's fee-for-service model backed by attacks on non-compliant shipping. Neither side's theory of control is yet proven.
• The tolls U-turn shows Gulf capitals retain leverage over Washington — and that the US wants regional buy-in, not unilateral rents. That is quietly deal-positive.
• Detainee release + Vance's ground-war exclusion + Ghalibaf's open door = both sides preserving an exit while escalating. The MOU is damaged (Trump: 'over') but the ~Aug 16 window (~31 days) still frames behaviour.
• Principal risk: an Iranian miscalculation at sea (another crewed tanker strike with mass casualties) or execution of the power-plant threat — either would jump the escalation ladder.

WATCHLIST — NEXT 72 HOURS
• Blockade enforcement incidents — any boarding, disabling with casualties, or Indian-flag vessel involvement.
• Bab el-Mandeb: Houthi follow-through would reprice Indian shipping, insurance and Suez trade instantly.
• Rupee 96.50; Brent $86.36 (Thursday morning high); Nifty 24,000 support; OMC hike signals.
• Trump's power-plant/bridges deadline language; UK IRGC proscription vote; any Qatar/Pakistan mediation restart.

CONFIDENCE
Market closes verified (HDFC Sky, Business Standard); Brent live per Investing.com/TradingEconomics. Blockade tallies per CENTCOM. Iranian casualty figures per Iranian officials — unverified. Analytical scores are estimates, not measurements.
